title: helm(private): stabilize values schema and init hooks for upgrade/rollback
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: private installer Helm chart had inconsistencies between the values schema and the init-hook templating which caused upgrade/rollback sequences to fail in some on-prem environments. This PR centralizes the values schema, tightens validation, and refactors init job and hook templates to be backwards-compatible while making behavior deterministic during upgrades and rollbacks.

What this changes: 1) Add a top-level values.schema.json for the redwood-private chart with explicit required fields and deprecation notes for legacy keys. 2) Refactor templates/init-jobs.yaml to make init jobs idempotent (check for existing PVs/K8s resources, adopt-name patterns) and annotate jobs so Helm recognizes them across upgrades. 3) Split hooks into upgrade-hook.yaml and rollback-hook.yaml with clear ordering and failure handling; add conditional logic to skip hooks when running in 'dry-run' or 'airgap' mode. 4) Update Chart.yaml and README with schema documentation and migration guidance. 5) Add a small e2e script and unit tests to validate upgrade->rollback round-trip in CI.

Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json added and validated locally with 'helm schema validate' - [x] init job idempotency tests added - [x] upgrade/rollback hooks separated and ordered - [x] migration docs added to chart README - [x] CI: unit + helm lint + integration upgraded and passing after rerun

Notes on compatibility: The schema marks legacy keys (privateInstaller.*) as deprecated and provides a migration snippet in README. The templating uses feature gates (values.private.featureFlags.enableNewInit) to allow safe rollout for customers who need time to migrate.

Why not a major version bump: The changes are designed to be opt-in for customers that flip the feature flag; default behavior preserves existing semantics. The schema will surface validation errors earlier for new installs but will not force changes on existing releases unless users opt into stricter validation.

Follow-ups: - Add a migration job in the installer operator to reconcile legacy keys in a subsequent PR (ENG-1482). - Expand e2e matrix to cover additional on-prem storage providers.

release_notes: Stabilize Helm chart for Redwood Private: add values schema validation, make init jobs idempotent, separate upgrade/rollback hooks, and include migration guidance. No forced breaking changes; opt-in feature flag for new init behavior.
